My understanding is that Jyhad cards should always be played as though
they have V:tES text, so it should not make any difference what card you
use. If this is not the case, then the Jyhad versions of Soul Gem of
Etrius must be very valuable, for they have 0 pool cost, as opposed to 2.

: When was Pulse of the Canaille ever cumulative?

I think you misunderstood him. Ritual Challenge is not cumulative as is
Pulse of the Canaille (not cumulative).

>(if they don't I'm in for a houserule saying exactly that :-)
>

Ritual Challenge (either version) gives the Gangrel upon whom it is
played hand damage of two (basically, even though it is 2 hand damage in
Jyhad and +1 in V:TES)

However, the card (again, either version) then says that ONLY ONE Ritual
Challenge may be played on a Gangrel. Thus, you *couldn't* play a Jyhad
one and then a V:TES one on the same vampire.

It's also important to note that a Jyhad Ritual Challenge on Zack North
(Jyhad version) will do nothing (he already *has* 2 hand damage), but a
V:TES version on a Jyhad Zack North will give him 2+1=3 hand damage, as
will a V:TES version on the V:TES Zack North.

When was Pulse of the Canaille ever cumulative?
I've only got Jyhad and Sabbat Pulses, so I can't say what the V:TES
Pulse actually says, but I would hope that it restricts the Pulse to
just one per vampire like the Sabbat versions.
Then at least it's marginally fair when you're going up against an
Auspex/Obfuscate bleed deck
